Chapter 6: Building Resilient Habits—Daily Practices for Long-Term Change.
So, now that you’ve got a foundation of grace and a clear vision for your sexuality, let’s talk about how to actually build resilient habits that support your growth for the long haul.
Think of habits as the scaffolding that holds up a building while it’s being built. They give you structure and stability, especially on those days when motivation is low or life just throws a curveball your way.
Building strong habits always starts small. Instead of trying to overhaul everything overnight, focus on steady, daily progress. It’s a bit like planting seeds every day—nothing dramatic at first, but over time, those seeds send down roots that help anchor new ways of thinking and acting.
There are a few daily practices that can really help make these changes stick.
First, there’s morning and evening reflection. Just take a few quiet moments at the start and end of your day to check in with yourself. You might look back on moments when you felt tempted, celebrate any victories, or think about where you want to grow. Journaling or even a bit of meditation can make this clearer—and it doesn’t have to take long.
Next, let’s talk about intentional routines. Creating a daily rhythm helps keep you busy with things that matter and naturally reduces those pockets of idle time that can lead to trouble. Maybe you plan out activities in advance, fill your schedule with meaningful work, or make time for regular exercise. The point is to set yourself up to succeed, right from the start.
Another big one is mindful self-talk. Pay attention to that inner voice—because it shapes how you respond when temptation strikes. If you notice negative thoughts like, “I’ll never change,” try gently swapping them out. Instead, remind yourself, “I’m learning and growing, one step at a time.” It really does make a difference.
And don’t underestimate the power of visual reminders. Placing notes, symbols, or objects where you’ll see them can reinforce your commitment to staying true to your deeper values. Sometimes, just a gentle nudge is all you need to stay focused.
Here’s a real-world example: imagine someone who struggles with late-night internet use. They might decide to turn off their devices by a set time every night, and use that time instead to read or catch up with a friend. At first, it takes effort. But after a few weeks, that new habit starts to feel natural, making it so much easier to say no to old patterns.
The most important thing? Approach habit-building with patience and self-kindness. Setbacks will happen, but every new day is a chance to start fresh. Over time, all these small choices add up—shaping a life that truly reflects the values and vision you’ve been working toward.
